title: Hosted API - embeddings + rerank demo (Search relevance walkthrough)
summary: Redwood AE + SE walked BrightNote through Hosted API embeddings and reranking endpoint workflows for improving site search relevance. Covered integration patterns, evaluation approach, cost/latency tradeoffs, security (SOC2, SSO, data retention), and next steps: bench test, pricing, and share security docs.
topics: Current search stack and pain points
Embeddings ingestion and vector store options
Reranking endpoint demo and API walkthrough
Latency vs cost tradeoffs, batching and caching
Security controls: SOC2, SSO, KMS, data retention
transcript:
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Evan from Redwood - AE on this account, and with me is Sana from our SE team. How's everybody doing?
[00:04] Alyssa: Good, thanks. Excited to see how rerank might help our product search. We've been getting noise in the top results, so hoping embeddings + rerank helps.
[00:12] Sana: Awesome — quick agenda, we'll do a short discovery, then a live demo of Hosted API embeddings and reranker, and end with next steps.
[00:20] Marcus: Sounds good. For context, we currently use an in-house TF-IDF baseline with a small ES cluster and Pinecone for semantic vectors, but relevance drift is an issue.
[00:28] Evan: Great, that's helpful. Couple qualification Qs — traffic patterns, p95 latency target, and any data residency constraints?
[00:35] Priya: We're about 50 queries/sec peak, p95 under 300ms would be ideal, and EU data residency for some customers.
[00:42] Sana: Noted. Hosted API can serve EU regions and we support per-tenant routing. We also have Dedicated and Private for stricter residency or audit needs.
[00:50] Alyssa: Cost is a big factor. Pinecone's vector store costs are creeping up; curious about per-query cost with embeddings + rerank.
[00:57] Evan: We'll send a cost-comparison later; quick note — reranking will add an extra inference step but often gives big lift so you can avoid expensive full-context generation.
[01:08] Sana: Ok demo time — opening the Console. (typing) The Hosted embeddings endpoint is straightforward: POST /v1/embeddings with your text batch, get back vectors. We recommend batching on ingestion; you can use continuous batching on our side if you want.
[01:26] Marcus: Question — do you recommend storing vectors in Redwood or external vector DBs?
[01:30] Sana: Both valid. Many teams use Redwood Hosted embeddings + external vector stores like Pinecone/Weaviate for large indexes. We also have short-lived vector storage patterns with caching to reduce egress. If you want unified ops, our Dedicated plan can host vector indices co-located with inference.
[01:47] Alyssa: For rerank, what's the input? Do we pass top-K documents?
[01:50] Sana: Exactly — typical flow: query -> retrieve top 50 from vector DB or ES -> call /v1/rerank with query + candidate snippets, returns scores + reordered list. Reranker payload size matters; we demo with 10-20 candidates to keep latency reasonable.
[02:04] Evan: I'm going to run a quick live example using your sample doc set we shared earlier (note: demo uses anonymized data).
[02:10] (screen share)
[02:14] Sana: Here we call embeddings for the query, use the stored vectors to get nearest neighbors, then call rerank. You'll see relevance jump for ambiguous queries.
[02:27] Alyssa: Looks promising. Any rough p95 numbers for reranking?
[02:30] Sana: For a 10-candidate rerank we typically see 50-120ms on GPU-backed Hosted profiles; CPU-backed can be 200-400ms depending on model size. These are broad ranges.
[02:41] Marcus: And cost per call?
[02:44] Evan: Depends on model choice and token lengths; we'll send model-specific pricing. In practice some customers use a cheaper embedding model + small rerank model to balance cost.
[02:55] Priya: Security — we need SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logs, and customer-managed keys for some PII.
[03:02] Evan: We are SOC2 Type II, support SAML/SSO, role-based access, and support integrations with KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer encrypted-at-rest and bring-your-own-key on some tiers; we'll attach the security pack.
[03:18] Alyssa: Great. Also curious about evaluation: how do you recommend measuring relevance improvements?
[03:22] Sana: Start with a holdout set of queries + ideal ranking; run baseline vs rerank. Use NDCG@10, MRR, and examine cases where rerank hurts — tie this into Redwood Optimize where you can run prompt/eval suites and set regression alerts.
[03:36] Marcus: Could you show an example of the rerank API request/response?
[03:40] (Sana pastes payload)
[03:44] Sana: Example POST /v1/rerank body: {"query":"...","candidates":[{"id":"doc1","text":"..."}, ...]} -> response: scores with normalized ranking. Note: payload truncation and tokenization differences can affect results; we surface warnings in the Console.
[04:00] Alyssa: There might be long product descriptions; how to handle long docs?
[04:03] Sana: Two patterns: index chunked passages with metadata, or use a hybrid approach where you do light retrieval then short-context rerank. Also prefix KV caching can help for repeated context.
[04:15] Evan: Another ops note — batching and caching drastically change unit costs. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching settings and quantization profiles to hit latency targets while reducing GPU utilization.
[04:27] Priya: If we do a pilot, what would success criteria look like?
[04:30] Alyssa: For us, 10-15% uplift in NDCG and elimination of top-1 irrelevant results for high-volume queries. Also p95 under 350ms on pilot traffic.
[04:40] Evan: We'll propose a pilot: 4-week bench with 2 weeks ingestion + 2 weeks A/B traffic, run automated evals, and supply dashboards.
[04:50] Marcus: Data retention: we need logs for 90 days and option to purge.
[04:54] Evan: Hosted includes configurable retention windows and redact/purge workflows. For stricter controls Dedicated or Private is better.
[05:02] (discussion continues, demo shows Console graphs)
[20:30] Alyssa: Quick interruption — how hard is integration for our engineers? Marcus: we have a small infra team, want to avoid heavy lift.
[20:40] Sana: Integration is often a 1-2 week engineering task for a basic flow: ingest embeddings at index time, keep a simple vector store, call rerank at query time. We have SDKs and quickstart templates.
[21:00] Evan: Any blockers around procurement/timeline?
[21:05] Priya: Q3 budget approval; pilot ideally starts mid-July. Procurement will need security docs and an MSA.
[21:15] Evan: We'll send SOC2 report, encryption/KMS docs, and a draft SOW/MSA.
[21:25] (more questions about model choices)
[28:10] Marcus: For model updates/rollouts, do you support canary or gradual rollouts?
[28:14] Sana: Yes — Console has rollout controls, canarying by percent, auto-fallback to previous model, and per-route configs.
[28:22] Alyssa: What about multivariate testing for rerank params?
[28:25] Sana: You can A/B routes or use Redwood Optimize to run parameter sweeps and record eval metrics.
[33:50] Evan: OK recap time — Pilot scope: ingest 1 month of queries, run index + rerank, A/B test on a subset of traffic, success metrics NDCG uplift and p95 latency target. Deliverables: security docs, pricing, pilot SOW.
[34:10] Priya: That works. Any expectations on Redwood side for support?
[34:14] Evan: AE + SE support during pilot, weekly check-ins, plus a dedicated Slack/Shared channel.
[34:22] Alyssa: Timeline: we'll confirm budget by end of June, pilot mid-July if approved.
[34:28] Evan: Great — I'll follow up with the materials.
[34:32] (call wraps, small crosstalk)
[34:40] Marcus: One last quick question — can you provide a sample benchmark on our sample corpus?
[34:45] Sana: Yes, we can run a bench if you share the anonymized dataset or we'll use the sample you already uploaded. Expect results in ~3 business days.
[34:55] Evan: Thanks all, we'll send next steps and security pack. Bye.
[35:00] (call ends)
